text:
ci-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: deploy-canary-failure for service=model-service (run=ci/4821) - healthcheck failed 502 x5. Logs hint at artifact digest mismatch: expected sha256:abc123... got sha256:def456... https://ci.example.com/runs/4821

eric: oncall (eric) here. acknowledging, taking lead.

alice: I saw a suspicious job earlier that retriggered image push to the canary tag. Investigating registry mutations now.

ben: If this is an image digest mismatch we should flip the canary feature flag off and pin to previous digest. Can someone prepare rollback command?

dana: I can flip flag and rollback. Quick check: are we using mutable tag `model-service:canary` or digest-pinned images?

alice: CI used `model-service:canary` for fast iteration. Looks like a parallel pipeline pushed a build and the digest changed mid-rolling-update.

eric: Ok. Plan: 1) flip feature flag to prevent traffic to canary 2) patch deployment to previous digest sha256:abc123 3) monitor errors.

ben: +1. Also notify SRE slack and Customer Success if we see >0.5% error spike.

alice: I'm grabbing the previous image digest from the registry manifest history. Found previous: sha256:abc123 (pushed at 2026-03-15T16:04:02Z).

eric: Performing actions now.

eric: ```bash
# disable canary traffic
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  https://flags.redwood.internal/api/flags/enable-canary-v2 -d '{"value":false}'

# pin deployment to known-good digest
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/model-service model-service=registry.redwood.com/model-service@sha256:abc123
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/model-service
```

alice: Flag set to false (confirm from flags console).

sre-bot: action_log: flag_update user=eric flag=enable-canary-v2 old=true new=false ts=1808501285

ben: Good. Patching to digest now?

eric: Patch applied. Rollout completed for canary replica set. Observability shows 200/200 health checks passed.

alice: Monitoring: error rate in us-west dropped from 1.8% to 0.05% over the last 3 minutes. Latency stable.

dana: Customer impact: quick analysis - spike affected ~420 unique requests (approx 0.3% global reqs) between 16:13-16:23 UTC. No SLO breach. Notified CSM to send proactive note for a few clients that hit 500s.

ben: Root cause hypothesis: mutable tag `canary` was updated by concurrent build pipeline -> race -> some nodes pulled new digest after rollout started -> digest mismatch with existing image layers -> container restart/healthcheck fail.

alice: Reproduced locally: if you push a new image with same tag while a rolling update is in-flight, kubelets may pull different digests on different nodes. Must avoid mutable tags for canary rollout.

eric: Short-term mitigation: enforce digest-pinning in rollout job and add registry manifest check step. Filed infra ticket for CI change.

alice: Ticket: INFRA-1147 created - "Enforce digest pinned deploys for canary and add manifest-lockstep in pipeline". Link: https://issues.redwood.internal/INFRA-1147

ben: Also adding an automated kill-switch in the deploy pipeline: if seen >2 distinct digests for same tag during rollout, abort and rollback automatically.

sre-bot: incident: created incidents/INC-20260315-4821 assigned eric, alice, ben. Severity: sev3.

eric: Leaving runbook and handoff to night oncall @dana. Notes: revert command above, flag already off, previous digest sha256:abc123 pinned, monitor for recurrence.

dana: Acknowledged, taking over. Will keep an eye on the metrics dashboard for the next 4 hours and follow up with postmortem.

ben: Thanks everyone. Follow-up items: INFRA-1147 (ci change), OPS-214 (automated abort on digest divergence), PM to coordinate client comms.

eric: Marking thread resolved once monitoring stable for 30m. Leaving at 18:10 UTC, handing to @dana.

sre-bot: incident_update: INC-20260315-4821 status=monitoring ts=1808501450

alice: small note: we should also consider certs for registry to speed up manifest fetch caching to avoid transient pulls.

dana: ack. I'll summarize in the postmortem and ping the release process owners in the morning.
